inventoryMethod.primaryBaseline: Delaware DNREC public-access and water-trail material, Delaware State Parks, First State National Historical Park, USGS, and the statewide tidal-fishing access inventory.
inventoryMethod.inclusionRule: Retain every distinct named moving-water corridor with an authoritative public-access lead. An access lead is not a route qualification.
inventoryMethod.qualificationRule: A route must have two lawful public endpoints, on/near-water coordinates, direct or clearly labeled proxy gauge evidence, route-specific flow/tide guidance, safety hazards, logistics, camping posture, and approved same-water imagery.
inventoryMethod.adjacentStateRule: Do not duplicate Pennsylvania, Maryland, or New Jersey records. Interstate water may be represented only when the Delaware endpoint and route-access posture are explicitly Delaware-scoped.
limitations: The statewide tidal-access inventory is an access baseline, not a complete canoe/kayak launch survey.
Tidal reaches require local tide, wind, traffic, weather, water-quality, and landing checks; a river gauge alone is insufficient.
Access-area coordinates are practical anchors and do not by themselves prove a currently usable wetted-edge entry.

prioritizedCorridors.finding: NPS publishes a bounded Smith Bridge-to-Thompson’s Bridge float with public access-area anchors, 1–2 hour estimate, hours/fees, and route-specific safety/low-flow caveats.

The current Delaware access inventory lists Newport, Churchmans Road, and 7th Street as public ramps. Two non-overlapping conservative packages are implemented: Churchmans-to-Newport upstream and Newport-to-7th-Street downstream, using direct USGS 01480120 same-reach telemetry and explicit traffic, bridge, debris, water-quality, facility-closure, and hard-boundary controls; do not infer access at bridges, private banks, or industrial shoreline.

DNREC identifies the public Reserve canoe/kayak launch and the DNERR management plan identifies The Rocks as a downstream Fish & Wildlife boat launch. NOAA station 8553069 and USGS 01483200 provide local tide and same-creek proxy context; preserve shallow-marsh, erosion, hunting-closure, CAP, private-bank, and current landing controls.

The statewide tidal-access inventory lists an Odessa access, but the current DNREC Appoquinimink watershed and public-access baseline did not establish a second lawful paddle endpoint with a route-specific operating package. Keep blocked until an independent public launch/take-out, on/near-water coordinates, and current tide/safety evidence are documented; do not infer access from road crossings, private banks, or Delaware River shoreline facilities.

The current Delaware access inventory lists Lebanon and Scotton as public Fish & Wildlife ramps, DNERR identifies both as canoe/kayak access and monitoring stations, and DNREC documents a tide-dependent St. Jones boating program. The implemented route remains a conservative planning reach with proxy USGS telemetry, local water-level/wind checks, water-quality controls, and hard endpoint boundaries.

The current Delaware tidal-access guide identifies Woodland Beach (Creekside) on Duck Creek as a public two-lane ramp with courtesy-dock support for kayaks and canoes, and DNREC’s wildlife-area map identifies the Duck Creek ramp and prohibits camping/open fires. The implemented package is intentionally a bounded same-launch tidal exploration because no independent second Duck Creek public paddle endpoint was established. It uses the official facility anchor for both launch and return, historical USGS 01483335 as clearly labeled same-creek stage proxy context, NOAA 8553501 tide predictions, route-specific shallow-channel/strainer/mud/wind/wildlife-area controls, nearby-basecamp-only camping, approved Delaware Tourism Woodland Beach imagery, and a hard return boundary before the bayside pier/Delaware Bay.

The current Delaware access inventory lists Canal Wildlife Area/C&D Canal as a fishing-pier-only access area with no boat ramp, while DNREC’s C&D Canal Conservation Area material documents a 14-mile commercial shipping route and trailheads rather than paddle launches. No two lawful Delaware paddle endpoints with on/near-water coordinates and route-specific operating evidence were established. Keep blocked until the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers or Delaware access managers document a paddle-appropriate endpoint pair, traffic/lock/current rules, and complete safety/logistics/camping/imagery/geometry evidence; do not infer a launch from trailheads, the fishing pier, or Maryland-side docks.

NPS describes the approximately 8-mile Roger C. Fisher Laurel River Park to Phillips Landing Broad Creek itinerary. The current Delaware inventory and DNREC’s reconstruction record support Phillips as a public three-ramp/canoe-launch endpoint; the route remains tide/wind dependent with the Nanticoke station clearly labeled as a proxy and the open Nanticoke boundary preserved.

The City of Milford identifies the Front Street public ramp, and DNREC/state materials identify the Cedar Creek public ramp at the Mispillion Harbor connection. The implemented route is a conservative approximately 10-mile tidal planning reach using NOAA 8556198 locally and USGS 01484100 only as a clearly labeled headwater proxy; preserve long-distance, tide/wind, shallow-mud, harbor-exposure, water-quality, and hard Cedar Creek boundary controls.

prioritizedCorridors.corridor: White Clay Creek / Red Clay Creek
prioritizedCorridors.finding: DNREC names these streams but notes that northern-stream access is largely through private property. Do not infer a route from road crossings or fishing access; reopen only with two lawful paddle endpoints and route-specific evidence.

The current Delaware access inventory and official FirstMap access layer establish Fort DuPont and Augustine Beach as separate public boat-ramp facilities with on/near-water coordinates. DNREC identifies Fort DuPont as a Branch Canal launch context and Augustine Beach as a managed boating-access area; state closure history requires an explicit dredging/maintenance check. The implemented package is an advanced Delaware-only Branch Canal-to-Delaware River-to-Augustine reach with tide/wind/commercial-traffic/cold-water controls, USGS 01482170 clearly labeled as nearby tidal proxy context, NOAA Delaware City tide/water-level guidance, nearby-basecamp-only camping, approved same-river imagery, and a hard Augustine endpoint. It does not claim Delaware Bay, an interstate landing, or an ordinary flatwater float.

The Town of Milton identifies the Memorial Park public boat-launch facility, and The Nature Conservancy documents a two-mile Broadkill canoe trail to its public non-motorized floating dock at Edward H. McCabe Preserve. The implemented route preserves a conservative approximate river-side dock anchor with explicit exact-dock/wetted-edge verification, labels USGS 01484272 as legacy-flow/water-quality proxy context without a numeric cutoff, and carries route-specific tide, shallow-water, private-dock, no-camping, daylight, and hard-endpoint controls.

Delaware State Parks’ official Savages Ditch–New Road water-trail map establishes an approximately four-mile Rehoboth Bay course for experienced kayakers, identifies both park access points, permits a loop or out-and-back from either end, and documents heat, wind, tide, nesting, private-property, and October–February waterfowl controls. The implemented package is bounded to this named course and does not claim Masseys Landing, Rosedale Beach, Indian River Inlet, the Atlantic Ocean, or an ordinary flatwater route.

The current Delaware access inventory lists a four-lane Seaford Nanticoke River ramp and an unimproved/carry-top Woodland Wharf Nanticoke access. DNREC documents Woodland Wharf’s public canoe/kayak dock, parking, bulkhead, and Fish & Wildlife management, while DelDOT documents the adjacent active ferry. The implemented lower-Nanticoke package preserves a separate hard Woodland Wharf boundary, uses USGS 01487000 as same-river proxy context, and carries route-specific tide/wind/current, ferry-cable, water-quality, camping, imagery, coordinate, and geometry controls.

The current official FirstMap Delaware access layer identifies three public Little Creek Wildlife Area boat-ramp features and a separate Little Creek Boating & Fishing Access concrete ramp with kayak/dock access. The implemented package uses a conservative Wildlife Area-to-town pair with official near-water facility anchors, clearly labeled nearby St. Jones tidal proxy evidence, DNREC’s waterfowl-season managed-water restriction and wildlife-area rules, route-specific shallow-marsh/tide/wind guidance, nearby-basecamp-only camping, public-domain nearby tidal-marsh imagery, and a hard town-ramp finish. It does not infer access from dikes, fishing piers, road crossings, impoundments, Port Mahon, Woodland Beach, or Delaware Bay.

The current Delaware access inventory identifies Piney Point as walk-in shoreline access for Pepper and Vines Creeks but no boat ramp. Treat this as an access lead only, not a qualified route; reopen with two lawful paddle endpoints, on/near-water coordinates, and route-specific operating evidence.

The current official FirstMap Delaware layer identifies public Strawberry and Sassafras Landing canoe/boat facilities, while DNREC’s Assawoman Canal Trail Concept Plan explicitly places both landings on Miller Creek. The implemented package is bounded to this named tidal-creek reach, uses direct USGS 01484701 Little Assawoman Bay water-level evidence with NOAA tide context, carries route-specific outgoing-tide, shallow-water, wind, boat-traffic, wildlife-area, and no-camping controls, and does not claim Mulberry/Dirickson Creek, the Assawoman Canal, open-bay, or interstate access.

The City of Lewes identifies a kayak/canoe and small-craft launch at Canalfront Park, and the City of Rehoboth Beach identifies the Grove Park Canal Dock behind the museum with short-term loading/unloading rules. NOAA provides the local Lewes tide reference and USGS 01484670 provides clearly labeled same-estuary proxy context. The implemented package is bounded at Grove Park and carries mandatory tide, wind, traffic, cold-water, private-bank, dock-condition, parking, closure, camping, coordinate, imagery, and geometry controls; it does not claim an open-water bay extension.

Current FWS refuge guidance directs paddlers west from Foord’s Landing because the eastern portion is heavily silted and not recommended for canoe or kayak travel. The official canoe-trail materials identify the western Brumbley Family Park/Waples Mill Pond launch, note a small fee and only six parking spaces, and document seasonal refuge/WMA ramp closures. The implemented package is therefore bounded to the western segment, uses approximate near-water anchors with mandatory field verification, carries shallow-channel/obstruction/wildlife/closure/private-launch controls, labels USGS 01484272 as nearby proxy context, and does not claim the closed eastern channel or an on-route camping posture.

The current FirstMap Delaware access layer identifies Bowers Beach as a public five-ramp concrete facility with large parking; the Town of Bowers explicitly identifies the surrounding Murderkill River as a kayaking setting; and USGS 01484085 is colocated at the public pier beside the ramps. The implemented package is intentionally a bounded same-launch tidal exploration with direct gage evidence and hard commercial/emergency-navigation, shoaling, tide, wind, cold-water, jetty, private-bank, and Delaware Bay controls. No unsupported upstream endpoint or open-Bay route is claimed.

reconciliationGate: Delaware is not complete until each prioritized corridor is implemented or has an explicit blocked/screened-out disposition with retryable evidence conditions, and the DNREC/park/tidal-access baseline has been reconciled against the route catalog.
